Update incorporating SLOOS: The April 2020 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey shows broad, rapid tightening in credit supply that reinforces and deepens the negative tone of the April 29 FOMC statement. Banks tightened standards and terms across C&I loans (including to middle‑market firms), CRE (nonfarm nonresidential, multifamily, construction/land development), and consumer credit (e.g., HELOCs), widened loan-rate spreads and increased costs on credit lines, and reported reduced risk tolerance with expectations of further tightening. Demand weakened notably in CRE and several business segments, with only partial offsets from stronger demand for government‑backed mortgages. These survey signals indicate a contracting availability of bank credit into 2Q20, consistent with impaired credit flow despite aggressive Fed easing and liquidity backstops. Net effect: downside risks to growth and employment are more pronounced than a policy‑only or FSR‑only read would suggest.
